claims.text: Sliding dynamically refines the HEA surface into a nanocrystalline or amorphous tribolayer.
Exposure of the transformed tribolayer to a reactive chloride-rich environment accelerates its oxidation.
The refined surface alters wear behavior through inverse Hall-Petch effects.
The transformed surface is more vulnerable to localized corrosion.
The dynamically transformed surface governs the coupled tribo-corrosion response.
The proposed material is an additively manufactured, initially coarse-grained, single-phase HEA.
The proposed HEA contains multiple principal elements.
The controlled comparison varies the environment between inert conditions and a chloride-containing aqueous solution while holding the mechanical sliding conditions constant.
High sliding shear causes surface grain refinement and amorphization.
Reactive environments during HEA wear can promote oxidation or mixed metal-oxide surface films that affect deformation and wear resistance.
The disordered tribolayer preferentially forms non-protective oxide films or brittle phases in chloride-rich solution.
Oxidation of the refined layer increases local corrosion rates.
Relative to the inert baseline, testing in chloride solution increases total degradation because of a higher corrosion rate.
The wear component may change only modestly or may improve slightly if a thin passivating oxide forms.
In an inert environment, degradation is dominated by mechanical wear and corrosion is minimal.
The predicted mechanism requires enough shear to generate the refined layer and enough reactive species to attack it.
The hypothesis may fail under low shear or when corrosion agents are absent or ineffective.
The balance between refinement-related wear changes and corrosion enhancement may depend on HEA composition and test conditions.
Wear volume, friction, tribolayer grain size and thickness, surface oxidation states, and electrochemical corrosion rate are proposed as measurable responses.
The mechanism is considered falsified if the chloride test shows neither increased corrosion nor the predicted surface changes or tribological differences relative to the inert baseline.
